about: Martsirt town lore lines for N3. lines: keyed by prop kind, prop tag or spot key; the game cycles through the variants. spots: tap points that are not props (tile coords, r = tap radius in m). Edit freely; no code change needed.

seat.ask: Sit here? The stone receiveth all who are weary.
seat.taken: Another keepeth this seat. Wait thy turn.
seat.sit: You sit. Let the hour pass without thee.

well: Here the parish drew water before the fire. Draw, and give thanks; the deep remembereth who drank.
A stone mouth over the dark. Three pails at dawn: one for the living, one for the drowned, one for the Seraph.
The rope is new; the stone is not. What is lowered here cometh up colder than it went.
bench: A seat of hewn stone, worn hollow by the waiting. Sit, and be counted among them that tarried.
Here the elders sat in judgment of small sins. The stone hath not forgotten the verdicts.
Cold stone, warm with the many. Rest thy feet; the road keepeth.
log: A felled bough, laid down for the weary. The wood holdeth the warmth of all who rested.
Sit by the ember, pilgrim. The log asketh no name.
chair: A joined chair, oak upon oak. Who sitteth here, let them hold their peace and hear.
The seat of one who keepeth watch. Sit not long, lest the watch fall to thee.
bonfire_main: The common fire of Martsirt. Feed it, and it keepeth the night at the door.
Ash upon ash. Each night the parish casteth one name into the flame, that it be not forgotten.
Zhera's fire was white. This fire is red, and it is ours.
bonfire: A traveller's fire. Warm thy hands, but turn thy back to it never.
Embers kept by the gate, lest the dark come in unannounced.
statue: Father Noll, rendered in salt. He called the fire down upon the drowned, and the fire found him also.
Touch not the salt. It was a man, and he was weighed, and he was found to have small sins.
Ysara washeth his feet each new moon. The salt weareth not away; it only weepeth.
notice: Notices of the parish, nailed in a row: tithes, a lost goat, the hour of the bell. Beneath, in a fainter hand: Pray for the salted.
The decrees of the watch. Read, and be warned; the gibbet heareth no appeal.
trough: Water for the beasts of the field. Even the oxen are served before the proud.
A trough of black water. The horses drink, and look at thee as if thou wert late.
anvil: Wolcen's anvil. Here iron is made to remember a shape. Strike true, for the metal heareth.
The face is scarred with ten thousand blows. Each was a prayer that something would hold.
shrine: An angel weepeth in the niche, her hands upon her face. The angels are bound and may not intervene; this is the shape of that binding.
Lay no coin here. She cannot take it, and she cannot refuse it.
stall: A chandler's stall. Tallow and wick, that the dark be held off one hour more.
Candles by the dozen, for the living and the salted alike. The price is the same.
chopblock: A block for the axe, scored a thousand times. Mind thy hand; the block keepeth no account of whose it was.
gibbet: The iron cage of the watch. Here the guilty hung until the crows had judged them.
The chain creaketh with no wind. Pass by, and say the short prayer.
font: The font of St. Noll. The water was salt once. Now it is only cold.
altar: Here the fire was asked for. Kneel if thou wilt; the altar hath heard worse prayers.
lych: The lych rest, where the dead are set down before the gate. Lay them here, and say the name aloud.
pew: Father Noll's flock sat here. They stand yet in the parish, white and still.
Worn smooth by knees. Sit, if thou canst bear the quiet of it.
glass: The one painted window left whole. The light through it falleth in colours no fire maketh.
Lead and coloured glass. The parish raised it before it called for Zhera's line.
candelabra: Tall iron and old tallow. Someone still lighteth these, and none will say who.
The flames lean toward the altar, though no draught moveth here.
carpet: A runner of old red cloth, worn to the weave where the flock walked to the altar.
Salt is ground into it. Zhera's fire leaveth salt, not ash.
effigy: A stone effigy, hands clasped. The face is rubbed away by kisses or by grief.
Someone hath left salt at its feet, as they leave it at the statue.
pulpit: Father Noll preached from here that the light would scorch the possessed. It took the flawed with them.
The book lieth open. The page is scorched at the edge and nowhere else.
rubble: The roof came down here. Cold light falleth through the hole.
Fallen beams and slate. Mind thy feet.
crypt_hatch: A stone hatch, chained and locked. Burnt hair and old incense. It was under the chapel first.
If the stone under the chapel warmeth, that is no hearth. Leave it.
church_sidedoor: The side door is barred from within. It stays so.
church_tower: The tower stair is fallen in past the first turn.
inn_bar: The Salted Kettle's bar. Mira keepeth it, and the taproom keepeth its own weather.
Rings of old ale on dark wood. Lean on it; everyone doth.
inn_hearth: A good fire, fed well. The one warm place in Martsirt that asketh nothing of thee.
The chimney draweth clean. Mira will have it no other way.
inn_keg: Ale from the cask. It tasteth faintly of the sea, as all things here do.
inn_table: Scarred tables, knife marks and dice burns. The talk is low and the cups are full.
inn_lantern: Iron and horn lanterns, smoke-black. They swing a little when the door goeth.
inn_cellar: The cellar hatch. Mira keepeth the key and goeth down alone.
inn_stairs: The rooms above are let. Not tonight.
inn_backdoor: The yard door, barred for the night.
